fe7c634054c2: MultiDatePick runs entirely inside your Salesforce org. Here is exactly how your data and your security are handled.
cd239174fd4c: MultiDatePick is a managed package of Lightning Web Components that runs inside Salesforce. It has no backend of its own, so there is very little to vet. Here is the short version.
b0995af65cc6: 100% native to Salesforce <t1>Nothing leaves your org</t1>
fe5c24b8d6e6: MultiDatePick runs completely inside your Salesforce org. It has no external servers, makes no outbound callouts, and sends no data to MultiDatePick or to any third party. Every date, time, booking, and record it touches stays in Salesforce, on your objects.
aed873881c41: Because nothing ever leaves your org, MultiDatePick operates under your existing Salesforce compliance and data-residency posture. There is no separate data processor to assess.
d63f26a9357c: <t1>Data sent to us:</t1> none. No telemetry, no analytics, no usage tracking.
06ddaf3ab5e3: MultiDatePick has passed Salesforce's AppExchange Security Review, the mandatory assessment every listed solution must clear. It covers static and dynamic code analysis, enforcement of access controls and record sharing, safe data handling, and confirmation that no secrets are hard-coded.
3394889ad28e: Runs with each user's own permissions
6a919de0bba8: All Apex executes in <t1>USER_MODE</t1> and validates object and field-level security (FLS) before every query and every write. The components can only read or change data the running user is already allowed to access. Sharing rules, FLS, and profile or permission-set access are always enforced. MultiDatePick never elevates a user's privileges.
1e6a84bc0bce: The package ships four permission sets. Assign the one each person needs, and nothing more. Records are created on the standard or custom objects and fields you configure, using each user's own access.
39bd260f8eff: The guest user of a public site. Read and create only, the most Salesforce allows a guest.
56e2b853bb62: <t1>What it reads and writes:</t1> date, time, and booking records on the objects and fields you configure.
62c5afdad19c: <t1>Where that data lives:</t1> your Salesforce org, on your objects. It never moves.
d543ae20b6e2: <t1>Saves are additive by default:</t1> new records are inserted; existing records are never deleted without an explicit action in the component.
